welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the early Nazi Party — from its 1919 founding to Hitler's failed 1923 putsch.
meta_desc: GCSE History — the founding and early years of the Nazi Party in Weimar Germany.
final_note: You learned how the NSDAP began, why the Beer Hall Putsch failed, and how Hitler wrote Mein Kampf in prison.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Nazi Party began in 1919 as the DAP.

Hitler joined that year and soon took it over. By 1920 it was renamed the NSDAP. It was just one of many extreme parties in chaotic post-war Germany.

On 8-9 November 1923, Hitler tried to seize power in Munich.

The Beer Hall Putsch failed. Police killed 16 Nazis. Hitler was arrested and sentenced to 5 years in prison — but only served 9 months.

walkthroughs.h2: Mein Kampf and a new strategy
walkthroughs.body_html:
In Landsberg Prison Hitler wrote Mein Kampf ('My Struggle').

It set out his ideas: hatred of Jews, Lebensraum (living space), and the need to destroy the Treaty of Versailles. He decided to seize power legally next time.
